references.text: God identifies Himself as the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob when He revealed Himself to Moses at the burning bush
God instructs Moses to tell the elders of Israel that the LORD, the God of their fathers, has appeared to him
Moses expresses concern that the people will not believe that the LORD has appeared to him
The people believed when they heard that the LORD had visited the children of Israel
God reveals Himself to Jacob as the God of Abraham and Isaac
Jesus quotes this formulation about the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in the discussion concerning the resurrection
Jesus refers to the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob from the burning bush
Jesus points to Moses at the thorn bush where the Lord is called the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob
Peter preaches about the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob who has glorified His servant Jesus
Stephen quotes God's words to Moses: I am the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob
Both verses are direct parts of the same revelation sequence at the fire and use an identical covenant formula to establish God's authority.
The verses form coherent parts of the same speech where the name of the covenant is used as a foundation for God's new action and eternal remembrance.
Both verses use the fathers' covenant as a theological guarantee for God's current actions (exodus vs. confirmation of the covenant).
Parallel revelation where God identifies Himself as 'the God of your fathers' to give comfort and promise blessing to a single leader.
